_comment: versionCode is the number Play counts uploads by. It must be higher than
the highest Play has ever accepted for com.phaserugbymanager.app, which
was 29. Before that: 28 was 1.5.7 internal testing, 27 was 1.5.6,
19 was 1.3.0, the first build with adverts, 5 Sep 2026; 17 was 1.2.9 and
15 the last TWA. Go up by one for every upload, record what Play accepted
here, and never reuse a number.
A VERSION CODE IS SPENT BY THE FIRST TRACK THAT TAKES IT, not by the
release reaching anybody. 28 went to Internal testing and Closed testing
then refused the same bundle - 'Version code 28 has already been used' -
because Play counts codes per app, across every track at once. Promoting
the existing release between tracks reuses the code; a second upload
cannot. 29 is the same 1.5.7 build, for the closed track.
30 IS 1.5.8, FOR THE CLOSED TRACK. 29 was the same 1.5.7 build, also
closed, 10 Sep 2026 - spent because 28 had already gone to Internal
testing and Play would not take the bundle a second time. Upload 30 to
Closed testing and nowhere else, then PROMOTE it if another track needs
it; a second upload of the same bundle cannot reuse the number.
31 IS 1.6.2, FOR THE CLOSED TRACK. Three versions were finished and never
uploaded - 1.5.9, 1.6.0 and 1.6.1 - and all three ship inside 1.6.2. NONE
OF THEM SPENT A CODE, because a code is spent by the first track that takes
a bundle and no bundle ever went up for any of them. That is the one saving
grace of a version that does not ship: it costs nothing as long as nothing
was uploaded. 31 is still the next number.
Upload 31 to Closed testing and nowhere else, then PROMOTE it if another
track needs it.
32 IS 1.6.3, the release-gate fixes (docs/archive/release-audit-v1.6.2.md). 31 was
uploaded to the closed track for 1.6.2 and is spent whether or not it was
promoted; never reuse it.
33 IS 1.6.4: the URC format, the women's World Championship, the forfeit
rule, the id counter in the save and the women's squad reconciliation.
34 WAS SPENT by an upload that never became a release (16 Sep 2026: Play
took the bundle, the release page then showed no bundle, and the next
upload of 34 was refused as already used). 35 IS 1.6.5: one calendar with
an invariant, the relegation playoff on finals day, Premiership relegation
restored, the runtime-brief fixes.
36 IS 1.7.0 (was written up as 1.6.9 before the version moved):
the campus art and the live infrastructure map, the ground
as a 0-5 ladder with upkeep and wear, territory and tactics by zone,
advantage, training-ground injuries, the goal-kicking ceiling, the
training pitch, the Boardroom, and the audit round - the suite had not
been run since the territory work and was failing in fourteen places;
181 engine probes and 57 browser harnesses are green on GitHub's own
runners at 405dbe1. Then, after the version moved to 1.7.0: the ranking
tables aligned to their hash, per-ask headlines for the eight boardroom
answers (four of them were printing a raw dictionary key in the inbox),
and the sacking repairs - a sacked manager no longer gets his old club's
news, no longer has his staff quietly running their week, and the board
that sacked him will not interview him for three months.
37 IS THE NUMBER 1.7.0 ACTUALLY SHIPS ON. 36 was written up above as
1.7.0 and is treated as spent - owner's call, 25 Sep 2026, on the Play
Console's own record. 35 is likewise treated as spent by the 1.6.5
upload. A code is spent by the first track that ACCEPTS a bundle and by
nothing else, which is the distinction that cost 34, so the rule stands:
check the highest accepted code on the Console before every upload and
never reuse a number.
38 IS 1.7.1: the match as something you watch (play between the lines,
phase shapes, kicks in the air, the TMO overturning tries in the engine,
the Broadcast camera and mini-map, the crowd under the match, half-time
and full-time cards) and three management features (medical jokers,
playing through a late knock, the home crowd on the tight calls).
38 IS ASSUMED FREE AND NOT YET VERIFIED: it assumes 37 was the last code
Play accepted. Check the highest accepted code on the Console before the
bundle is built - scaffold.sh reads this file - and never reuse a number.
39 IS 1.7.2: the men around the ball (tackles to ground with a ruck over
them, the scrum driving and wheeling, the lineout lift, carded players
walking off, replacements jogging on). 39 IS ASSUMED FREE AND NOT YET
VERIFIED: codes only have to rise, so it is right whether or not 38 was
ever uploaded, but check the highest accepted code on the Console first.
40 IS 1.7.3: players who talk back (answers read against personality,
four new reasons to knock) and the Major Rugby Competition. 40 IS ASSUMED
FREE AND NOT YET VERIFIED: check the highest accepted code on the Console
first. Codes only have to rise, so 40 is right whichever of 38 and 39 went up.

41 IS 1.8.0 (1.7.4 and the planned 1.8.1 folded in, never uploaded; the name stays PHASE: Rugby Manager): the two-layer match engine (player contests under the team), commentary with live stats and the pitch for tries and big moments, a fairer board with a first-season honeymoon, tired sides that concede more and a bench that pays, tablet and iPad layouts, opening titles, the six-language review, a new career that never overwrites a save, and the PHASE Discord linked from the menu, About and the bug report. 41 IS ASSUMED FREE AND NOT YET VERIFIED: check the highest accepted code on the Console first.

40 IS 1.8.1 (the planned 1.9 folded in): the manager remembered (decisions that come back as stories, former players met), a club identity that emerges from how it is run, dressing-room bonds and rifts, the opposition report with a match plan and post-match findings, career history that acts (rivalries that grow, legends, annals, returning to an old club), a drilled library of attacking moves, transfer windows enforced, a yearly academy sign-or-release decision, development focus for five, and the tester-note fixes. THE CONSOLE'S HIGHEST ACCEPTED CODE WAS 36 on 29 Sep 2026 (owner, from the Play Console): 37 to 41 above were written up but never accepted by Play, so none of them is spent. 40 was chosen over 37 to leave a margin (owner's call). 1.8.0 was never uploaded; it ships inside 1.8.1.

41 IS 1.8.2: styles (five attack, five defence), the manager's desk, recruitment detective work, the career arc (rival coaches, reputation, chairmen, ambitions, eras), the dressing room, development projects, season priorities, tactical depth (weather, conditions, specialist positions, pod shapes), the playbook arms race and a calibrated analyst, nine new moves, rebuilt highlight clips, drawn flags and four more rewarded favours. Codes only have to rise: 41 is right whether or not 40 (1.8.1) was uploaded. Check the Console's highest accepted code before building.

versionName comes from the root package.json.
billingLibrary is the Play Billing Library version PhaseBilling.java is
written against. Play refuses anything below 8.0.0 (learned 4 Sep 2026).
reviewLibrary is the Play In-App Review library behind PhaseBilling.review() (1.9.3).
